MINUTES
  GENERAL PLAN ADVISORY COMMITTEE MEETING
  FEBRUARY 2, 2021

1.  CHAIR SCHMITZ called the meeting to order at 6:00 p.m.

2.  ROLL CALL

  COMMITTEE MEMBERS PRESENT:  Addleman, Arata, Bayer, Carrese, Corman,
  Friedman, Medawar, Schmitz, Shinn,
  Zuckerman

  COMMITTEE MEMBERS ABSENT:  Carman, Buresh, Seamans, Silvano

  STUDENT MEMBER PRESENT:  Michael Scandaliato

  STAFF MEMBERS PRESENT:  Greg Grammer, City Manager
  David Wahba, Director of Community Development
  and Public Works
  Jeannie Naughton, Planning Manager
  Kelley Thom, Associate Planner
  Carol Corea, Administrative Assistant

  ALSO PRESENT:  Surabhi Barbhaya, Senior Planner, Michael Baker International
  Natalie Chyba, Fehr & Peers
  Seth Contreras, Fehr & Peers
  John Muggridge, Fehr & Peers

3.  APPROVAL OF MINUTES

NONE

4.  AUDIENCE ITEMS WRITTEN/ORAL COMMUNICATIONS NOT ON AGENDA

NONE

5.  DISCUSSION ITEMS

A.  MOBILITY ELEMENT

Seth Contreras, Fehr & Peers provided a brief recap of the last GPAC meeting (January 19,
2021). The goal of the last meeting was to receive feedback on the proposed Mobility Element
topic areas along with the goals and policy focuses to develop the Mobility Element.

Natalie Chyba, Fehr & Peers provided a brief summary from the last GPAC meeting, including an
overview of how the Mobility Element is structured, the existing Transportation Element “issues”,
and the changes that are being proposed for the 2040 Mobility Element.

Mr. Contreras provided an overview of the five Mobility Element topic areas.

  •  Transportation Network & Safe Street Design
  •  Vehicular Circulation
  •  Pedestrian Circulation
  •  Recreation Trails & Bicycle Circulation
  •  Transit & Transporation Demand Management

The GPAC Members participated in “break-out” sessions to discuss the following topic areas:

  •  Group 1: Recreation Trails & Bicycle Circulation
  •  Group 2: Transit & Transit Demand Management

The group facilitators provided a summary on the discussions from the “break-out” sessions, including
those from the meeting of January 19, 2021.

 GENERAL PLAN ADVISORY COMMITTEE MEETING
  1
 MINUTES, FEBRUARY 2, 2021
 Ms. Chyba provided a summary from the Transportation Network & Safe Street Design topic area
discussion. A few of the talking points, included:

  •  Roadway Classification – There was consensus to maintain individual neighborhood
  characteristics and avoid blanket statements that dictate uniformity.
  •  Complete Streets Goals – This is State mandated; the group decided that there is a balance
  to what is recommended and what is safe given roadway topography.
  •  Commercial District Street Design – It should be much easier to get around the whole district
  without having to get into your car.
  •  Utilizing Repaving to Add Improvements – When repaving the road making sure that safety
  improvements are added.
  •  Curbside Management – This should go hand in hand with the general re-visioning of the
  district and there is not enough burb space to allocate effectively.
  •  Goods Movement – This is important due to the topography constraints in the City.
  •  Emergency Vehicle Access – There was discussion on evacuation routes and the preference
  is to evacuate by car, especially when considering animals/horses.

Mr. Contreras provided a summary from the Vehicular Circulation topic area discussion.

  •  Maintaining efficient flow
  •  Traffic Calming – Adding traffic calming features to address road safety. There was a
  suggestion to work with the HOA’s regarding striping and signage.
  •  EV Parking Spaces – How to incorporate electric vehicle parking
  •  Parking Requirements – Parking is an important part of the travel experience; consider design
  of parking spaces; anticipate future needs

CHAIR SCHMITZ asked for clarification on parking design and anticipating future needs. Mr. Contreras
stated that in terms of the parking spaces to allow flexibility for smaller and larger size vehicles. There
is an ongoing parking study that is being completed as part of the General Plan Update and this will
be factored in.

Ms. Chyba provided a summary from the Pedestrian Circulation topic area discussion.

  •  Context-Sensitive Sidewalk Design – Making sure to keep the rural/equestrian feel of the City.
  •  Crosswalk Policy – Developing a crosswalk policy to address concerns around high traffic
  speeds and students, who are not always paying attention. The policy should be tailored to
  the City.
  •  Tree Canopy/Shading – This especially resonates in the commercial district and could add
  charm.

COMMITTEE MEMBER BAYER stated that there is a concern from someone who walks her dog and
waits almost five minutes to cross the street at both Hawthorne Blvd. and Crenshaw Blvd. Another
concern is where there is a yield sign and a crosswalk; drivers often only look one way and do not see
the pedestrian in the other direction. Ms. Chyba stated that in regards to the pedestrian crossing, there
could be changes to the signal timing, by extending the pedestrian walk-sign intervals. In regards to
the driver turning right and the conflict with the pedestrian, design elements could be considered to
make vehicles approach the turn at a slower speed.

Surabhi Barbhaya, MBI, explained that there was discussion on exploring signalized intersections near
schools because kids may not look around when crossing.

COMMITTEE MEMBER FRIEDMAN stated that crosswalks should go beyond the County’s criteria for
crosswalks. In addition, it’s important to look to surrounding land uses; there are a lot of seniors who
live near Peninsula Center and cross Silver Spur Road, for example, and this should be considered.

Ms. Chyba provided a summary from the Recreation Trails & Bicycle Circulation topic area discussion.

  •  E-Bike Share – Think critically where to implement this and make sure that safety is prioritized.
  Partnering with the right vendors.
  •  Bike Parking – Discussed locations in the commercial district that already have bike parking
  and expand that to promote biking as an option. Explore bike repair stations. Also, making
  sure to separate e-bike parking and traditional bike parking.
  •  Install Bike Racks on Buses – The PV Transit buses have bike racks but the shuttle buses do
  not.
  •  Context-Sensitive Bike Design
  •  Recreational Trails – There was discussion about the Highridge trail and having more that are
  like it.
  •  Equestrian Facilities – This was about disseminating information on amenities, including
  parking and water for horses.
  •  Developing a Bike Network – Continuing to promote the existing bike network.

 GENERAL PLAN ADVISORY COMMITTEE MEETING
  2
 MINUTES, FEBRUARY 2, 2021
 Mr. Contreras provided a summary from the Transit & Transporation Demand Management topic
area discussion.

  •  Getting to School – There was discussion on PV Transit and how to make this a more efficient
  for students. Encourage more shared rides to school. There was concern with walking and
  biking due to the topography of the City.
  •  Getting Around Town – How to encourage multimodal options. Working with PV Transit to
  target specific locations in the off-peak hours. Exploring autonomous vehicles in the
  commercial district.
  •  Commuting – There are a lot of work-from-home residents and looking at specific destinations.
  In addition, looking to discounted rates for seniors.

COMMITTEE MEMBER CARRESE suggested getting corporate sponsors or using grants to help with
marketing and advertising. Printed information on routes and distributing them to churches, schools,
and HOAs.

6.  COMMITTEE ITEMS / FUTURE AGENDA ITEMS

Mr. Contreras stated that more feedback has been received and the next step is to prepare the draft,
moving on to the implementation program, and the environmental review.

Ms. Barbhaya stated that there will be one more GPAC meeting. After the final meeting, the
information will be gathered and they will proceed with the production of the General Plan Update.
There will be a joint meeting with the Planning Commission and City Council meeting, where the
GPAC will be invited, on the Housing Element. Once that is done, the General Plan Update will
be out for public review in July or August 2021.

7.  ADJOURNMENT

CHAIR SCHMITZ thanked the committee and adjourned the meeting at 7:18 p.m.

Respectfully submitted,  Approved,

____________________________________  _____________________________
Carol Corea, Administrative Assistant  Velveth Schmitz, Chair

 GENERAL PLAN ADVISORY COMMITTEE MEETING
  3
 MINUTES, FEBRUARY 2, 2021
